page: Amazon Web Services m8g.4xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by the AWS Graviton ARMv9 processor utilizing Neoverse-V2 cores clocked at 2.8 GHz. The instance is configured with 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs, maintaining a single thread per core without simultaneous multithreading. It provides 64.0 GB of memory, equating to 4.0 GB per vCPU, with an L3 cache size of 36 MB, 2 MB L2 cache, and 64 KB L1 data cache. This instance type includes no local bundled storage, requiring remote EBS volumes, and has no discrete GPU accelerators. Baseline networking throughput is provisioned at 8 Gbps.

Benchmark results highlight strong memory subsystem performance alongside balanced compute capabilities. The instance scored within the top 10% on the PassMark memory suite (3213.67), demonstrated by large-block uncached read speeds of 296.67 GB/sec and write speeds of 133.88 GB/sec in the top 25%. Decompression throughput is also elevated, reaching 200.91 GB/sec in multi-threaded bzip3 tests. General compute tests reflect steady mid-tier output, with Geekbench yielding a single-core score of 1867.0 and a multi-core score of 15796.0. Database operational throughput scored in the top 25% on PassMark with 24099.5 operations.

Hardware tradeoffs include the absence of x86-specific instruction sets like AVX, AVX-512, and AMX, making workloads dependent on those vector extensions unsuited for this platform. Furthermore, medium model LLM prompt processing fell into the bottom 25% at 31.24 tokens/sec, and high-tier (70B) LLM evaluation yielded no viable results, indicating limitations for larger AI inference workloads. The ARM64 architecture delivers cost efficiency through dense single-thread core execution and superior memory throughput per core relative to equivalent standard x86 general-purpose nodes.

The m8g.4xlarge instance is optimal for memory-sensitive enterprise applications, relational and key-value database operations, multi-threaded data compression, microservices architectures, and high-throughput static web serving.

It is equipped with 16 dedicated physical cores (16 vCPUs) clocked at 2.8 GHz with a 1:1 thread-to-core mapping, paired with 64.0 GB of RAM. The instance lacks local storage and discrete GPUs, relying on an 8 Gbps baseline network link. Benchmark testing reveals top-tier memory performance, achieving a PassMark memory score of 3213.67 and robust uncached read/write bandwidth in the top 25%. Decompression and database operations also score above average. Tradeoffs include modest large-model LLM inference capabilities and the absence of x86 vector extensions like AVX-512.
